title: First and Last Purchase Date per Customer
description: For each customer, find their **first purchase date**, **last purchase date**, **total number of purchases**, **total amount spent**, and the **number of days between first and last purchase** (their tenure as a buyer).
solution_sql: SELECT customer_id, MIN(purchase_date) AS first_purchase, MAX(purchase_date) AS last_purchase, COUNT(*) AS total_purchases, SUM(amount) AS total_spent, MAX(purchase_date) - MIN(purchase_date) AS days_as_customer FROM purchases GROUP BY customer_id ORDER BY customer_id

test_cases.description: 4 customers with purchase history summary. C1: 4 purchases over 64 days. C4: 1 purchase, 0 days tenure.

hints: Use MIN(purchase_date) for the earliest order and MAX(purchase_date) for the most recent — both computed within GROUP BY customer_id.
Subtracting two DATE values in PostgreSQL returns an integer representing the number of days between them.
explanation: GROUP BY customer_id with MIN and MAX extracts purchase history boundaries. C1: first=Jan 5, last=Mar 10, 4 purchases totaling $725, tenure=64 days. C2: Jan 10–Feb 8, 2 purchases, $330, 29 days. C3: Jan 25–Mar 5, 3 purchases, $525, 39 days. C4: single purchase Feb 20, $120, 0 days tenure (first=last). This foundation underpins cohort analysis and customer lifetime value (LTV) calculations.
